assessments.reasoning: I retrieved Oracle's governing Java SE 21 JLS from its edition-specific HTTPS locator and matched the frozen source SHA-256 before inspecting every listed paragraph. JLS §17.4.4 supplies the synchronizes-with edge from a write to every later read of the same volatile variable in synchronization order. Section 17.4.5 turns that edge into happens-before and explicitly states the volatile field rule. The distinction between the variable and a field declaration preserves the source's same-variable requirement. The targeted comparison found no applicable contradiction.

challenge.method: Compare different volatile variables, the same instance declaration on distinct objects, an earlier read, intervening same-variable writes, and a compound read-modify-write. Check the read-from constraint in §17.4.7.
challenge.results: A volatile write directly orders each subsequent read of its own variable. Distinct instances of an instance field supply distinct variables. With write w1, then intervening write w2, then read r to one variable in synchronization order, w1 still happens-before r while synchronization-order consistency rules out r observing w1. The edge gives no indivisibility to a compound update.

limitations: The claim concerns a happens-before edge between accesses to one variable. The rule does not imply that a read sees a particular earlier write or make a sequence of operations atomic.
